Documentation → Administration → Trust store

Trust store — CAs SATOM accepts from devices

Import your company Root and Intermediate CAs so appliances signed by them can be connected to with TLS verification switched on, and test any device against the store.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Certificates & Trust → Trust store (URL /settings/#tab-catrust)

What is it?#

The trust store holds the certificate authorities SATOM believes when it connects to an appliance. Appliances signed by your company CA cannot be verified against the public root store alone, so without this page the only option was to switch certificate checking off. Import your Root CA and any Intermediate CA here and those appliances can run with verification on.

ℹ️Note — Two sides of TLS

Node TLS is the certificate SATOM presents. The trust store is the list of issuers SATOM accepts. Public roots stay trusted — this store adds to them, it never replaces them.

What does it do?#

  • Stores CA certificates in the database, so both HA nodes and the database backups carry them.
  • Classifies each certificate from its own contents: root when subject equals issuer, otherwise intermediate — whatever box you pasted it into.
  • Accepts only CA certificates; a device's own self-signed leaf is rejected with the reason.
  • Builds a bundle file of the public roots plus every enabled CA. Appliance connections with SSL verification switched on validate against that bundle.
  • Lists incomplete chains — enabled intermediates whose issuer is not in the store.
  • Content shows exactly what was stored (decoded fields and PEM) with Copy PEM and Download .pem.
  • Disable keeps a CA on record but drops it from the bundle; Delete removes it.
  • Test a device against the store opens a TLS connection to an appliance and names the cause when it fails: untrusted issuer, host name mismatch or expired certificate.

Requirements#

  • The CA certificates in PEM (one or several concatenated) or as a single DER file.
  • For the test: appliances visible in the current ADOM.
  • To make use of the store, the appliance must have SSL verification switched on — Verify SSL Certificate on its edit form (see Appliances).

Permissions#

The trust store requires users.manage (Administrator). The Certificates & Trust group of Settings is only offered to administrators, and the /settings/trust-store/… endpoints answer 403 to other users. See Permissions.

How to use#

Add a root and an intermediate CA#

  1. Open Settings → Certificates & Trust → Trust store.
  2. Under Add certificate authorities, optionally type a Name (default: the certificate's CN) and a Note (for example where the CA comes from and who owns it).
  3. In the Root CA box, paste the PEM into PEM text or choose a file under …or upload a .pem / .crt / .cer file, then click Save root CA.
  4. In the Intermediate CA box, do the same and click Save intermediate CA.

Each Save sends only its own box (plus Name and Note) and clears that box afterwards. The message line reports Saved: …, Updated: …, Rejected … — <reason> and, when the certificate's role differs from the box you used, <name> was filed as root, not intermediate — the role comes from the certificate itself (a root is its own issuer).

💡Tip — Save both

An intermediate whose issuer is missing imports cleanly and then fails every handshake with unable to get issuer certificate. Save the root too — the Incomplete chain warning tells you when one is missing.

Review the store#

The table lists Name, Role, Subject, Issuer, Expires, Status and Actions. Status is trusted, <N>d left (less than 30 days to expiry), disabled or expired.

Above the table:

  • Verifying against the public root store only. No private CA is enabled, so a privately-signed appliance cannot be verified. — nothing private is enabled yet.
  • Active bundle: <path> — public roots plus the enabled CAs below. — the bundle is live.
  • Incomplete chain. These intermediates have no issuer in the store or the public roots, so a device relying on them will still fail to verify: followed by each intermediate and the issuer it needs.

Inspect a CA (Content)#

Click Content on a row. The Certificate content dialog shows Role and status, Subject, Issuer, Serial, Valid from, Valid until (UTC), Public key, Signature, SHA-256 and SHA-1 fingerprints, every extension (with a critical badge where set), Note, Added (when and by whom) and the full PEM. Use Copy PEM or Download .pem, then Close.

Disable, enable or delete#

  • Disable / Enable toggles the CA in or out of the bundle immediately; the record stays.
  • Delete asks for a second click (Confirm delete, within four seconds) and removes the record.

Test a device#

  1. Under Test a device against the store, choose the appliance. Each entry shows its host, port, product and verify ON / verify OFF.
  2. Click Test TLS. Nothing is changed on the device or in SATOM.
  3. Read the result: Verified or Not verified with the reason, and — when the device answered — Presented, Issuer, Names covered, Expires, TLS (protocol and cipher), Chain trusted and Hostname matches, followed by advice.
  4. When it says the appliance can run with verification on, edit the appliance and tick Verify SSL Certificate.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Name Label for the CA; defaults to the certificate CN. With several certificates in one Save, (root) / (intermediate) is appended; an existing name gets #2, #3 No Example Corp CA
Note Free text, up to 500 characters No Issued by the security team
Root CA — PEM text / file Trust anchor; .pem, .crt, .cer, .der One box per Save -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----…
Intermediate CA — PEM text / file One or several concatenated One box per Save —

Saving a certificate that is already stored (same SHA-256 fingerprint) updates it in place; its name is kept and the note is replaced only if you typed one.

Example#

🧪Example — Turn verification on for a company-signed FortiWeb

  1. fweb-01 was registered with verification off because its certificate is signed by Example Issuing CA, which chains to Example Root CA.
  2. Paste Example Root CA into Root CA → Save root CA → Saved: Example Root CA.
  3. Paste Example Issuing CA into Intermediate CA → Save intermediate CA. No Incomplete chain warning appears.
  4. Test TLS on fweb-01 → Verified — certificate chain and hostname both verify.
  5. Edit fweb-01, tick Verify SSL Certificate, save.

Result#

  • A trusted_cas record per CA, carried by database replication and backups.
  • A rebuilt bundle file on each node: the public roots followed by every enabled CA.
  • Audit log entries trust_store.import (counts of imported, updated and rejected), trust_store.toggle and trust_store.delete.
  • Appliance API connections with verification on, hypervisor connections with verification on, and the attack-log reader all validate against the bundle.

Troubleshooting#

"Rejected … — not a CA certificate (basicConstraints CA:FALSE or absent) …"#

Possible causes - You imported a device's own certificate (a self-signed leaf or a server certificate) instead of its CA. - A very old root without the basicConstraints extension.

Solution — import the CA that issued the device certificate. If the device presents a self-signed certificate there is no CA to trust: re-issue its certificate from your company CA, or keep verification off for that appliance.

Verification — the CA appears in the table as trusted.

"Paste or choose a root CA certificate first."#

The box you saved is empty (same message with intermediate). Paste PEM text or choose a file in that box.

"Could not parse the PEM: …" / "Not a certificate. Expected PEM text starting with '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----', or a DER file."#

Possible causes — truncated or edited PEM, a private key or CSR instead of a certificate, or a file in another format.

Solution — export the CA certificate again as PEM (Base64) or DER and retry.

The test says "issuer is not trusted: …"#

Import the CA named after The certificate says its issuer is: in the advice, plus any intermediate above it, then test again.

The test says "chain is trusted but the hostname does not match: …"#

The CA is fine; the name SATOM connects to is not in the certificate. Set the appliance's host to one of the names listed under Names covered, or re-issue the device certificate with that name in its SAN.

The test says "the device certificate expired on …"#

Re-issue the appliance certificate. Trusting a CA cannot rescue an expired certificate.

The test says "the device presents a SELF-SIGNED certificate — there is no CA to trust"#

Nothing to import. Re-issue the device certificate from your company CA (then import that CA), or keep verification off for this appliance.

The test says "could not open a TLS connection: …"#

This is reachability, not trust: check the appliance host, port and that the box is up.

An intermediate signed by a public root is listed under "Incomplete chain"#

The check only looks for the issuer among the CAs in this store. If the issuer is a public root, the chain still verifies (public roots are part of the bundle); confirm with Test TLS, or import that root as well to clear the warning.

Advanced#

Advanced How the bundle is used
  • The bundle file is written atomically under the installation's PKI directory (trust/ca-bundle.pem) and rebuilt only when the set of enabled CAs changes. With no enabled CA, SATOM uses the stock public root list.
  • The answer is cached for 30 seconds per worker process; import, toggle and delete reset it in the process that handled the request, so other workers follow within that time.
  • If the bundle cannot be built, verification falls back to the public roots — never to no verification.
  • An appliance with verification off is not affected by the store at all.
Advanced What the test does

The test reads the presented certificate without validating it, then performs two handshakes against the current bundle — one with host name checking off, one with it on. The combination names the cause. It runs against the appliance's configured host and port (443 if none), and only appliances visible in your current ADOM can be selected.
